e-13143.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Linear Equations and Inequalities
e-13143.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \{n \in \mathbb{N}: 5n - 2 \leq 21 \}.$
e-13143.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $5n - 2 \leq 21.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}5n-2 & \le 21 \\ 5n & \le 23 \\ n & \le \frac{23}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The positive integer solutions of the inequality above are $1,2,3,4.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{1,2,3,4\}.
$$

e-13176.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
e-13176.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \{x \in \mathbb{Z}: x^2 - 9 \lt 0\}.$
e-13176.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $x^2 - 9 < 0.$

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-9 & <0 \\ {x}^{2} & <9 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & <\sqrt{9} \\ |x| & <3 \\ -3<x & <3\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $0,\pm1,\pm2.$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{ 0, \pm 1, \pm 2\}.
$$

e-13178.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
e-13178.problem: List the elements of the set $A=\{k \in \mathbb{Z}: |k-1| \leq 4 \}.$
e-13178.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $|k-1| \leq 4.$ So, we first need to solve for $k{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|k-1|\le 4 \\ -4\le k-1\le 4 \\ -3\le k\le 5\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the above inequality are $-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5.$ 

Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A = \{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,4,5 \}.
$$

e-13179.problem: List the elements of the set $A = \left\{ x\in \mathbb R \: :\:  \tan \left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = 0  \right\}.$
e-13179.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\tan \left(\dfrac{\pi x}{2}\right) = 0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi x}{2} & =n\pi  \\ x & =2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in\mathbb Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x = 0,\, \pm 2 ,\, \pm 4,\, \pm 6,\, \ldots
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A= \{0,\, \pm 2 ,\, \pm 4,\, \pm 6,\, \ldots\}.
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in Z:5n+25=10}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the equation $5n+25=10.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5n+25 & =10 \\ 5n & =-15 \\ n & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution is $n=-3,$ which is an integer.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$

The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the equation 5n+25=10.

5n+25=105n=−15n=−3

The solution is n=−3, which is an integer.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

A={−3}.

A={-3}.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $C={n\in N:24<4n}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $24<4n.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}24 & <4n \\ 6 & <n\end{aligned}
$$

The positive integer solutions of the inequality above are $7,8,9,10,11,12,….$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:4n+7=-9}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the equation $4n+7=-9.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4n+7 & =-9 \\ 4n & =-16 \\ n & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

However, since $-4\notin N,$ we conclude that the set $A$ contains no elements. Hence, $A=∅.$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Which set is equivalent to B={n∈Z:2n−11<−4}?

a
{…,−4,−3,−2,−1,0}
b
{0,1,2,3}
c
{…,−2,−1,0,1,2,3}
d
{−2,−1,0,1,2,3}
e
{…,−3,−2,−1,0,1,2}
Submit

decision.explanation: Adding 11 gives 2n<7, so n<7/2. The integer solutions are all integers at most 3, extending indefinitely in the negative direction.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $B={n\in Z:2n-11<-4}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integers that satisfy the inequality $2n-11<-4.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2n-11 & <-4 \\ 2n & <7 \\ n & <\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The integer solutions of the inequality above are $3,2,1,0,-1,-2,….$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
B={…,-2,-1,0,1,2,3}.
$$

content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in {R}^{-}:3{x}^{2}\le 27}?$
content.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the negative real numbers that satisfy the inequality $3{x}^{2}\le 27.$ 

So, we first need to solve our inequality for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & \le 27 \\ {x}^{2} & \le 9 \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}} & \le \sqrt{9} \\ |x| & \le 3 \\ -3\le x & \le 3\end{aligned}
$$

The negative real numbers that are solutions to the inequality above are $x\in [-3,0).$ Therefore, the given set can be written as 

$$
A=[-3,0).
$$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $B={x\in R:{x}^{2}-5=0}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are real numbers that satisfy the equation ${x}^{2}-5=0.$

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =5 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5},$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
B={\pm \sqrt{5}}.

content.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Quadratic Equations and Inequalities
content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $B={x\in R:{x}^{2}-5=0}?$
content.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are real numbers that satisfy the equation ${x}^{2}-5=0.$

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5 & =0 \\ {x}^{2} & =5 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5},$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
B={\pm \sqrt{5}}.
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:3{x}^{2}+27=0}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $3{x}^{2}+27=0.$ 

So, we first need to solve our equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}+27 & =0 \\ 3{x}^{2} & =-27 \\ {x}^{2} & =-9 \\ x & =\pm \sqrt{-9} \\ x & =\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={n\in N:|n+6|<1}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the natural numbers that satisfy the inequality $|n+6|\le 1.$ So, we first need to solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|n+6|<1 \\ -1<n+6<1 \\ -7<n<-5\end{aligned}
$$

The above inequality does not have natural solutions.

Therefore, the set $A$ is a null set:

$$
A=∅.
$$

a

b
{±1}
c
[−1,7]
d
{7}

decision.explanation: The equation |x-3|=4 means x-3=4 or x-3=-4, giving x=7 or x=-1. Thus A={-1,7}.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:|x-3|=4}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $|x-3|=4.$ So, we first need to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|x-3| & =4 \\ x-3 & =\pm 4 \\ x & =3\pm 4 \\ x & =-1,7\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-1$ and $x=7,$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-1,7}.
$$

content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:|x-3|=4}?$
content.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $|x-3|=4.$ So, we first need to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|x-3| & =4 \\ x-3 & =\pm 4 \\ x & =3\pm 4 \\ x & =-1,7\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-1$ and $x=7,$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-1,7}.
$$

after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={k\in Z:|4k-2|\le 6}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the integer numbers that satisfy the inequality $|4k-2|\le 6.$ So, we first need to solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|4k-2|\le 6 \\ -6\le 4k-2\le 6 \\ -4\le 4k\le 8 \\ -1\le k\le 2\end{aligned}

$$
A={0,\pm 1,2}.

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:|2x+5|=13}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the real numbers that satisfy the equation $|2x+5|=13.$ So, we first need to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|2x+5| & =13 \\ 2x+5 & =\pm 13 \\ 2x & =-5\pm 13 \\ x & =\frac{-5\pm 13}{2} \\ x & =-9,4\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-9$ and $x=4,$ and both of these solutions are real numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-9,4}.
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={q\in Q:|2q|=6}?$
after.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the rational numbers that satisfy the equation $|2q|=6.$ So, we first need to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|2q| & =6 \\ 2q & =\pm 6 \\ q & =\pm \frac{6}{2} \\ q & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $q=-3$ and $q=3,$ and both of these solutions are rational numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$

Question 15
?

Which set is equivalent to A={q∈Q:|2q|=6}?

a
{−3,3}
b
[−3,3]
c
{0,1,2,3}
d
{−3,−2,−1,0}
e
{3}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The elements of the given set are the rational numbers that satisfy the equation |2q|=6. So, we first need to solve for q: |2q|=62q=±6q=±62q=±3

The solutions are q=−3 and q=3, and both of these solutions are rational numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as A={−3,3}.

content.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={q\in Q:|2q|=6}?$
content.worked_solution:
The elements of the given set are the rational numbers that satisfy the equation $|2q|=6.$ So, we first need to solve for $q:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|2q| & =6 \\ 2q & =\pm 6 \\ q & =\pm \frac{6}{2} \\ q & =\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $q=-3$ and $q=3,$ and both of these solutions are rational numbers.

Therefore, we can write the given set as

$$
A={-3,3}.
$$

after.name: Question 16
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R\,:\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)=0}?$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡(4x)=0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{\pi }{2},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \pi ,\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\,\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{\pi }{2},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \pi ,\,…}.
$$

decision.explanation: Sine equals 1 when πx=π/2+2nπ, so x=1/2+2n for any integer n. These rational solutions are …,-7/2,-3/2,1/2,5/2,9/2,… .

after.name: Question 17
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in Q\,:\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)=1}?$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)=1
$$

are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\pi x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ \pi x & =\pi (\frac{1}{2}+2n) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}+2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…}.
$$

Question 17
?

Which set is equivalent to A={x∈Q:sin⁡(πx)=1}?

a
∅
b
{12,32,52,72,…}
c
{±12,±32,±52,±72,…}
d
Z
e
{…,−72,−32,12,52,92,…}
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the solutions to the equation sin⁡(πx)=1 are given by πx=π2+2nππx=π(12+2n)x=12+2n where n∈Z.

Substituting different values of n, we see that the solutions are x=…,−72,−32,12,52,92,…

Therefore, our set A is equivalent to A={…,−72,−32,12,52,92,…}.

content.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Trigonometric Equations
content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in Q\,:\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)=1}?$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi x)=1
$$

are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\pi x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi  \\ \pi x & =\pi (\frac{1}{2}+2n) \\ x & =\frac{1}{2}+2n\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={…,-\frac{7}{2},-\frac{3}{2},\frac{1}{2},\frac{5}{2},\frac{9}{2},…}.
$$

after.name: Question 18
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=-1}?$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)=-1
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =\pi +2n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{n\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{5\pi }{4},\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={\pm \frac{\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{3\pi }{4},\,\pm \frac{5\pi }{4},\,…}.
$$

decision.explanation: Sine is zero at integer multiples of π, so 2πx=nπ gives x=n/2 for every integer n. All these values are rational, yielding zero and all positive and negative multiples of 1/2.

after.name: Question 19
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in Q\,:\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)=0}?$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)=0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi x & =n\pi  \\ 2x & =n \\ x & =\frac{n}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm 1,\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\,\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm 1,\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,…}.
$$

content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in Q\,:\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)=0}?$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi x)=0
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2\pi x & =n\pi  \\ 2x & =n \\ x & =\frac{n}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm 1,\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\,\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm 1,\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,…}.
$$

a
{0,π2,π,3π2,…}
b
{…,−32,−1,−12,0,12,1,32,…}
c
R
d

e
N
Submit

decision.explanation: Cosine equals 1 at integer multiples of 2π. Thus 2x=2nπ gives x=nπ for every integer n, yielding zero and all positive and negative multiples of π.

after.name: Question 20
after.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=1}?$
after.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=1
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =2n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi \end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \pi ,\,\pm 2\pi ,\,\pm 3\pi ,\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\pm \pi ,\pm 2\pi ,\pm 3\pi ,…}.
$$

Question 20

Which set is equivalent to A={x∈R:cos⁡(2x)=1}?

a
{0,π2,π,3π2,…}
b
{…,−32,−1,−12,0,12,1,32,…}
c
R
d
{0,±π,±2π,±3π,…}
e
N
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Notice that the solutions to the equation

cos⁡(2x)=1 are given by

2x=2nπx=nπ

where n∈Z.

Substituting different values of n, we see that the solutions are

x=0,±π,±2π,±3π,…

Therefore, our set A is equivalent to A={0,±π,±2π,±3π,…}.

content.knowledge_point: Sets Defined Using Trigonometric Equations
content.problem: Which set is equivalent to $A={x\in R:\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=1}?$
content.worked_solution:
Notice that the solutions to the equation

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)=1
$$

 are given by

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =2n\pi  \\ x & =n\pi \end{aligned}
$$

where $n\in Z.$ 

Substituting different values of $n,$ we see that the solutions are

$$
x=0,\,\pm \pi ,\,\pm 2\pi ,\,\pm 3\pi ,\,…
$$

Therefore, our set $A$ is equivalent to 

$$
A={0,\pm \pi ,\pm 2\pi ,\pm 3\pi ,…}.
$$
